title: Count Number of Possible Root Nodes
summary: Alice owns an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1.
statement: Alice owns an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1. The tree is described by a 2D integer array edges, where each edge is represented as [ai, bi]. Bob can make guesses about the parent-child relationships by choosing two distinct nodes u and v, claiming u is the parent of v. His guesses are documented in a 2D integer array guesses. Alice confirms at least k of his guesses are correct. Given edges, guesses, and k, determine the number of nodes that could be the root of Alice's tree. If no such tree exists, return 0.
constraints: edges form an undirected tree on nodes zero through n-1.
Each directed guess [parent,child] predicts one edge orientation.
Return how many root choices make at least k guesses correct.
hints: First root the tree at zero and count correct directed guesses.
Moving the root across edge parent-child reverses only that edge's orientation.
Subtract a guessed old orientation and add a guessed reversed orientation while recursing.
Every node is reached once with its exact rerooted count, so thresholding those counts returns all possible roots in linear time.
editorial: Every node is reached once with its exact rerooted count, so thresholding those counts returns all possible roots in linear time.

tests.explanation: Roots zero, one, and four each satisfy at least three guesses.
Only root zero preserves the guessed orientation, so the answer is one.
